metaTitle: Kando: learn a language from videos in that language
metaDescription: Kando is an open-source desktop app that transcribes a video on your computer, translates each line with the AI model you choose and plays it with bilingual subtitles.
metaImageAlt: Kando's library: the most recent film, the jobs in progress and the films in the library
heroTitle: Learn a language from videos in that language
heroLead: Paste a video link or drop a video file on the window. Kando downloads online videos, transcribes the speech on your own computer, translates every line, and plays the video with the original and the translation on screen together.
heroReleaseNote: Builds for macOS and Linux are on GitHub Releases. On Windows:
shotLibraryAlt: The library: the most recent film, the jobs in progress and the films in the library
howTitle: From a link to bilingual subtitles
howLead: Every video goes through the same steps, one job after another. A job that fails says why and links to the setting that fixes it.
stepAddBody: Paste a link from YouTube, Bilibili or another site, or pick or drop a video file (mp4, mov, mkv, webm and others).
stepDownloadBody: yt-dlp downloads the video into your library. Local files are transcribed where they are, not copied.
stepTranscribeBody: whisper.cpp recognizes the speech on your own computer and detects the spoken language.
stepTranslateBody: Any OpenAI-compatible model translates the transcript line by line into the language you choose.
stepWatchBody: The original video plays with each line and its translation on screen together, and a bilingual .srt is saved next to it.
featuresLead: A native desktop app written in Go, with no web view. Your videos and subtitles stay ordinary files on your disk.
featureOnDeviceBody: Speech is recognized locally with whisper.cpp. Settings › Speech Recognition lists seven whisper models, from Tiny (77.7 MB) to Large v3 (3.1 GB), and downloads the one you choose.
featureModelBody: Lines are translated by EveryAPI by default, or by any OpenAI-compatible chat API, with presets for OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, DeepSeek, xAI, Mistral, Qwen, Kimi, Zhipu GLM, SiliconFlow, Ollama and LM Studio.
featurePlayerBody: Show both lines, the original only, the translation only or none. Shift the subtitles in 0.1-second steps, change their style, search every line, split the video into 4 to 12 equal clips in the side panel, and resume where you stopped.
featureFoldersBody: A library is a .kando folder of ordinary files: the video, its cover and its .srt subtitles. Manage it in Finder or a file manager, keep several, and switch between them from the sidebar.
featureSitesBody: Kando downloads through yt-dlp, so a link from any site it supports will do. Help › Supported Websites… lists them all, with their logos.
sitesStripLabel: Some of the websites Kando downloads from
featureAgentsBody: The Kando program is also a command line: kando add <link> queues a video, opening Kando first if it is not running, and kando mcp is an MCP server through which an AI agent can add videos, follow jobs and read subtitles. In a browser with WebMCP, this page also gives agents tools to check whether Kando supports a website and to find the right download.
featureLanguagesBody: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese and Korean. Kando starts in Simplified Chinese; change it in Settings › General, and the window switches at once.
featureUploadBody: After signing in with Google, upload a film's video and bilingual subtitles from the player to Cloudflare R2, Amazon S3, Alibaba Cloud OSS, Tencent Cloud COS or any S3-compatible store. Signing in needs your own Google OAuth client ID in KANDO_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, and uploading needs your storage's keys; see the README's Configuration section. Nothing is uploaded automatically.
featureShortcutsBody: Playback, subtitles and windows have shortcuts, listed in a cheat sheet (⌘/) and in Settings › Keyboard Shortcuts.
playerTitle: The original and its translation, together
playerLead: Each translation sits above its original line, and Style › Bilingual Order can put the original on top instead. The side panel lists every line: click one to jump to it.
shotPlayerAlt: The player with bilingual subtitles and the side panel's list of lines
settingsLead: Settings shows which programs Kando found, downloads the whisper model you pick, and is where you choose the AI service that translates.
settingsGeneralCaption: General: the open library, the interface language, the version and the programs Kando found.
shotSettingsGeneralAlt: Settings › General: the open library, the interface language, the version and the programs Kando found
settingsAICaption: AI Service with EveryAPI selected. Test Connection sends a short request to check the settings.
shotSettingsAIAlt: Settings › AI Service with EveryAPI selected
startLead: Kando runs on macOS, Windows and Linux. On macOS and Linux it downloads the programs it needs by itself the first time it opens.
startDownloadBody: Builds for macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) and Linux (x86-64 and ARM64) are on GitHub Releases. There is no Windows build yet, so on Windows build from source.
startDownloadSigned: Releases newer than 0.5.1 are signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so macOS opens Kando without a warning.
startToolsBody: The first time Kando opens, it downloads whichever of these programs is missing, and its Getting Started guide shows the progress. Ones you already installed, such as with Homebrew, are used as they are. If a download fails because yt-dlp is out of date, Kando offers Update and Retry.
toolFfmpeg: extracts the audio and decodes the picture and the sound
startToolsOther: On Windows Kando does not download them yet: install the same programs with your package manager and make sure they are on PATH.
startSetup: Then download a whisper model in the guide or in Settings › Speech Recognition. For translation, sign in once with the EveryAPI CLI (everyapi auth login), or enter another provider's model and API key in Settings › AI Service (Ollama and LM Studio need no key).
startBuildNote: The build is written to apps/kando/build for the platform you are on: on macOS, an ad-hoc signed Kando.app and a .dmg; on Windows and Linux, an executable and installer packages. Without make, as on a stock Windows, run go tool mygo build apps/kando from the repository root.
startReadme: Read the full guide in the README
